summary_paragraph: A 34-year-old woman was admitted after an outburst in which she threw a table, reporting intense emotional dysregulation, racing thoughts, and poor sleep. She was diagnosed with a mixed episode of bipolar disorder and admitted for stabilization. During her 15-day psychiatric stay, she was restarted on lithium and initiated on an antipsychotic, with close monitoring of mood, medication levels, and chronic conditions including hypothyroidism and endometriosis-related chronic pain. She acknowledged ongoing alcohol and sedative use, expressing motivation to address substance use post-discharge. Over time, her mood stabilized, she engaged in treatment planning, and she demonstrated improved coping strategies. She was discharged with a comprehensive follow-up plan including psychiatry, pain management, and addiction counseling, showing hope and commitment to recovery for the sake of her child and herself.
problems: Bipolar disorder, current episode mixed, unspecified
